summary: Eugen Hultzsch worked in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Leipzig and completed his habilitation under Georg Bühler at Vienna. He served as Government Epigraphist in India (~1886–1903) and held a chair at Halle-Wittenberg (1903–1925).

Eugen Pander was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied at Polytechnikum Riga. In 1881, he was a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan.
Eugen Prym was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Bonn from ~1862 to 1867. He later held an academic post at the University of Bonn from ~1870 to 1908.
Eugen Wilhelm worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under August Schleicher. He served as a professor at the University of Jena from ~1869 to 1923.

Eugene Obermiller specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studying under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1921–1925). He worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1928–1935) and as Section Secretary at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1935).

Eugene Watson Burlingame worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying under Charles Rockwell Lanman in 1909. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1908–1914), Johns Hopkins University (~1914–1917), and Yale University (~1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Wu Hung and John M. Rosenfield, taught at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997), and became the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art at Harvard University (~2005).
Eugeni d'Ors was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Barcelona (~1897–1903) and Universidad Central (~1903–1905). He later held a post at Universidad Central from ~1927 to 1954.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (~1920–1924) and held a post there (~1928–1939). He later served at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~1945–1969) and headed Indology at the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies after studying under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He served at the Court of Appeal of Paris (1824), the Société Asiatique (1826–1832), and taught at the Collège de France (1832–1852).
Eugène Jacquet was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He pursued his studies under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat (~1828–1832) and Eugène Burnouf (~1832–1838).

Eugène Tisserant was a scholar in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He completed studies at Lycee Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, École du Louvre, and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1904–1907).

Eun Hino is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's course at the University of Tokyo. Hino served as a project researcher at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2014) and as an assistant professor at Musashino University (~2015).
Eun Maeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as president of Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earning a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. Cho served as an assistant professor at the University of Michigan until 2004, when Cho became professor at Seoul National University.
Eunyoung Choe is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at Korea University. Choe is attested as an HK professor at Geumgang University from 2013 to 2015.

Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She is attested in 2006 as a professor emeritus and former department chair at the University of Alberta, and as Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary.
Eva Neumaier-Dargyay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Rigzin. She held an academic post at the University of Calgary.

Eva Tichy is an Indologist and linguist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1974–1981) and completed her habilitation at Marburg (~1982–1989). She held the chair of Indo-European linguistics at the University of Freiburg from 1993 to 2017.

Eva Wilden is an Indologist who completed her MA, doctorate, and habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1986–2003). She served at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (2003) and became Professor of Tamil Studies and Manuscript Studies at Hamburg in 2017.
